mbm-1551.clue: Nobody gets a turn until the roof goes on.
mbm-1551.quote: The cardboard lid of our game split in half. I built a tiny train station from it, complete with a roof. Our pieces wait there between games. Someone always leaves the horse on the platform.

mbm-1552.clue: I keep exactly one shoe clean.
mbm-1552.quote: My brother and I run opposite loops around the lake. When we meet, we tap the insides of our shoes. Last Sunday we traded muddy footprints at ankle height.

mbm-1553.clue: My partner can tell the music by the teacups.
mbm-1553.quote: We practice on the pastry shop floor after closing. For a quickstep, we take the china down from the shelf. The one time we forgot, the teacups joined us on percussion.

mbm-1554.clue: I can fit the whole river into one tin.
mbm-1554.quote: After each rafting trip I paint one bend inside a sardine tin. The latest one has a pebble for the rock where our guide ate lunch. They stack nicely on the windowsill.

mbm-1555.clue: I made sure my robot could kneel.
mbm-1555.quote: Grandpa repairs shoes, so I built him a model robot with a brush on one knee and a tin of polish on the other. It stands in his window wearing the shiniest boots in town.

mbm-1556.clue: Turn my spoon over before you use it.
mbm-1556.quote: I pressed a rosemary sprig into the wet clay of a spoon rest. My sister flips it over after every meal to check that the little branch hasn't grown.

mbm-1557.clue: That third controller is the secret to our duet.
mbm-1557.quote: I play the melody in our music game and my cousin taps the bass. Our littlest fan holds an unplugged controller and takes a bow with us. He has the best timing of the three.

mbm-1558.clue: There's a little hole in the blue handkerchief.
mbm-1558.quote: I tried to pull a daisy from my sleeve and caught it on the lining. Granddad passed me his old blue hankie. Now I thread the stem through its buttonhole and he gets the flower at every show.

mbm-1559.clue: Check the sugar bowl after dessert.
mbm-1559.quote: I promised to make Aunt Ruth's ring disappear. She slipped it back onto her hand while I was busy flouring a lemon. I cut the fruit open and she applauded wearing the evidence.

mbm-1560.clue: I save the pink chalk for one handhold.
mbm-1560.quote: The wall at the gym has a hold shaped like a pig's nose. When I finally reached it my belayer made such a convincing snort I almost sat down laughing.

mbm-1561.clue: The coin trick is much louder in the rain.
mbm-1561.quote: I used to make pennies vanish into a felt hat. On a rainy night I borrowed a colander. Every penny went ping, and the kids made me do the trick again just to hear it.

mbm-1562.clue: My jam jar has very fancy shoes.
mbm-1562.quote: I shaped a clay pot on three short feet so the jam wouldn't leave rings on our table. Mum painted each foot a different sock. She turns it every morning to choose today's pair.

mbm-1563.clue: I left room in the border for a paw.
mbm-1563.quote: After I finished quilting, our dog backed into a saucer of washable paint, then sat on the border. I stitched around the little green paw. Visitors ask where I got the pattern.

mbm-1564.clue: My rabbit act takes one carrot and no rabbit.
mbm-1564.quote: I covered a carrot with a scarf and announced a rabbit would appear. My little cousin reached under it and nibbled the tip. His two bent fingers took a remarkably good bow.

mbm-1565.clue: I leave one side of the cassette empty.
mbm-1565.quote: Mum mailed me her half of our old duet, with gaps exactly where I come in. I sing along in the kitchen. On the last chorus you can hear her laughing before I miss the note.

mbm-1566.clue: I keep my oldest ski pass under the wax.
mbm-1566.quote: I found a yellow lift pass in Dad's bag. We took the same chair up and held his old photo beside the trees. The bent pine in the middle had grown taller than both of us.

mbm-1567.clue: The dog in the signal box has a punctual tail.
mbm-1567.quote: At the crossing I sketched the same little terrier for a month. Every time the local train passed his window, one ear stood straight up. I finally caught it in my notebook.

mbm-1568.clue: I cut the moon out of the cuff.
mbm-1568.quote: Dad's last pair of concert trousers had a silver stripe down the leg. I pieced it into a night-sky quilt and used the shiny cuff for the moon. The trousers got an encore.

mbm-1569.clue: I keep some pages upside down on purpose.
mbm-1569.quote: The woman who runs our corner laundry guessed my mystery ending from three wet drafts on a line. I turned the last chapter face down. She handed me a peg and said she'd wait for paperback.

mbm-1570.clue: I polish the wrong end of my trophy.
mbm-1570.quote: The bowling league gave me a little cup after my first clean game. Its wobbly base spins nicely. At home we use it to decide who gets to bowl first next week.

mbm-1571.clue: I pack a second pair of laces for the trail.
mbm-1571.quote: The sign blew off our fork. We tied my orange laces around the post so the walkers behind us could find the way. A week later somebody had fashioned them into a perfect bow.

mbm-1572.clue: My beach blanket has a little sundial.
mbm-1572.quote: I set a shell at the end of my paperback's shadow when I lie down. When the shadow gets past it I turn over, put another shell in place, and start the next chapter.

mbm-1573.clue: Our shortest fielder never drops a catch.
mbm-1573.quote: My cousin stuck a beach umbrella upside down in the sand for a wicketkeeper. The first ball landed in it and stayed put. The umbrella earned a spot in our team photo.

mbm-1574.clue: I know the lock keeper's tea by the smell.
mbm-1574.quote: On Sunday I paddle the canal with two mugs in the bow. The keeper lowers a pot on a string from the bank, and I float there till the gates open. Sometimes I wish they took longer.

mbm-1575.clue: I've got a finish line you can eat.
mbm-1575.quote: My daughter drew the end of my route in chalk outside the greengrocer. On market days the owner lays a banana across it for me to break. I've never lost that race.
